Layouts

Source: R/layout.R
layouts.Rd

A layout arranges the panels of a montage. The columns of the images tibble that you map to x and y in tidymontage() (such as condition) arrange blocks of panels; the layout decides how the channels and views of each block are arranged:

Usage

layout_grid(channel = c("auto", "x", "y"), view = c("auto", "x", "y"))

layout_hero(
  hero = NULL,
  side = NULL,
  position = c("right", "bottom", "left"),
  labels = TRUE,
  stack = FALSE
)

Arguments

channel, view

For the grid: the axis ("x" or "y") for channels and views. "auto" uses an axis that no other column is mapped to.

hero, side

For the hero layout: the big panel and the small panels of each block, chosen with panel(). By default, the hero is the merge (or the first channel) of the main view (full image or crop), and the side panels are the single channels of the zoom (or of the main view).

position

For the hero layout: where the small panels go.

labels

For the hero layout: label the small panels with what distinguishes them (usually the channel), in the header font, outside the images: below them for position = "bottom", beside them otherwise, rotated like ggplot2 facet strips. Long labels wrap onto two lines. Stacked side panels line up across blocks, so they are labelled once: on the left of the first column when below the hero, and below the last row when beside it.

stack

For the hero layout: stack the small panels so that each is as long as the hero's edge, for strips such as a 15 x 4 um zoom. Below the hero, the strips are as wide as the hero and placed one under the other; beside it, they are as high as the hero and placed side by side. The side panels can have another aspect ratio than the hero, but all side panels share one.

Value

A layout specification for tidymontage() or adjust_layout().

Details

  • layout_grid(), the default, puts channels and views on the rows and columns of a grid. Each channel and view is placed automatically on a free axis, unless you map channel or view to x or y yourself.

  • layout_hero() shows one big panel per block, for example the merge of a crop, next to a strip of small panels, for example the single channels of a zoom.

Layouts are like themes: switch between them with the layout argument of tidymontage() or with adjust_layout(), without changing the mapping.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tidymontage(images, x = condition, layout = layout_grid(channel = "x"))
tidymontage(images, x = condition, layout = "hero")
tidymontage(images, layout = layout_hero(side = panel(view = "crop"), position = "bottom"))

# a big merge with zoom strips of each channel below it
tidymontage(images, layout = layout_hero(position = "bottom", stack = TRUE)) |>
  add_zoom(width = 15, height = 4)
} # }
